Cash position and operating cash flow generation will be critical metrics to scrutinise — given AIM's stage of development, a deteriorating cash runway or elevated burn rate could signal near-term capital raise risk, while improving cash conversion would materially de-risk the investment thesis.

Forward guidance embedded in the results announcement will set the tone for FY27 expectations — any upgrade to revenue or earnings outlook, new contract wins flagged, or strategic initiatives disclosed will be key triggers for re-rating by buy-side analysts updating their models.

announcements.headline: Appendix 4E & Annual Report
summary: Annual report filing (Appendix 4E) is a mandatory market-sensitive disclosure, signalling full-year financials are now available — investors should scrutinise revenue, NPAT, and any impairment charges relative to prior year and consensus expectations to gauge whether AIM has delivered on guidance.

Key metrics to assess include cash position and operating cash burn rate to determine runway adequacy, alongside any changes to receivables or deferred revenue that may indicate underlying business momentum or deterioration.

Forward outlook commentary within the annual report — including management guidance, strategic initiatives, and any going-concern disclosures — will be critical in setting near-term market expectations and determining whether current valuation is justified.

announcements.headline: FY26 Results Presentation
summary: FY26 results presentation is market sensitive, signalling material disclosure that will directly reprice IGO — investors should brace for significant volatility given the company's ongoing restructuring of its lithium portfolio and the challenging spodumene price environment that has weighed on earnings throughout the year.

Key metrics to watch include EBITDA margins from the TLEA (Tianqi Lithium Energy Australia) joint venture, cash generation from the Forrestania nickel assets wind-down, and any impairment charges against lithium assets — prior periods have seen substantial write-downs that materially impacted reported net profit.

Outlook guidance on capital allocation will be critical: the market needs clarity on whether IGO will defend its dividend, pursue further asset divestments, or redeploy capital into new commodity exposures as it navigates a structurally oversupplied lithium market — any reduction in distributions or balance sheet deterioration would be a meaningful negative catalyst.

announcements.headline: FY26 Financial Results
summary: FY26 full-year results represent a critical reset moment for IGO following a prolonged downturn in lithium prices — investors will scrutinise EBITDA margins and whether Greenbushes spodumene operations have returned to meaningful positive cash flow after successive writedowns and impairments that battered the balance sheet in FY24-25.

Key metrics to watch include net debt position, realised lithium prices versus spot, and any revision to the TLEA (Tianqi Lithium Energy Australia) joint venture dividend policy — with IGO's cash generation heavily reliant on Greenbushes throughput and offtake pricing, any guidance upgrade or cost reduction at the mine level would be a material re-rating catalyst.

Forward outlook on capital allocation is pivotal — the market will assess whether IGO restores a dividend, accelerates exploration at its nickel/copper portfolio, or pursues M&A to diversify away from lithium exposure; management commentary on the lithium price recovery timeline and FY27 production targets will set the near-term sentiment trajectory.

announcements.headline: Appendix 4E
summary: IGO's Appendix 4E (preliminary final report) is market-sensitive, signalling material financial outcomes for FY2025 that could meaningfully reset consensus expectations — investors should watch closely for headline NPAT, EBITDA margins, and any impairment charges tied to the embattled Greenbushes lithium and TLEA joint ventures.

With lithium prices remaining deeply depressed throughout FY2025, IGO faces a high probability of significant write-downs on its lithium assets and potential dividend reduction or suspension, directly pressuring net asset value and income-focused institutional holders.

The key forward indicators to assess are: (1) any revised guidance or strategic repositioning away from lithium exposure, (2) the balance sheet strength and net cash/debt position given project-level cash burn, and (3) whether management signals asset divestments or JV restructuring as a pathway to capital preservation.

announcements.headline: Financial Results for the Half Year Ended 30 June 2026
summary: Half-year financial results for the period ended 30 June 2026 are market sensitive, signalling material information that is likely to move SNZ's share price — investors should scrutinise revenue trajectory, EBITDA margin trends, and any guidance revision against prior consensus expectations.

Key metrics to watch include cash burn rate and balance sheet liquidity, as these will determine whether SNZ requires near-term capital and whether operating leverage is translating into improved unit economics across its core business segments.

Forward outlook commentary and any FY2026 full-year guidance update will be critical — reaffirmation or upgrade of targets would support a re-rating, while any downgrade or cautionary language on macro headwinds could compress the multiple in the near term.

announcements.headline: FY26 Financial Results Presentation
summary: FY26 results presentation for Mineral Resources (MIN) arrives at a critical juncture — the company is navigating elevated debt levels, asset divestment programs, and restructured lithium operations, making balance sheet trajectory and net debt figures the primary focus for institutional investors assessing solvency risk.

Key metrics to scrutinise include EBITDA margins across Mining Services and Lithium segments, progress on the Onslow Iron haul road ramp-up, and any update on debt reduction targets — prior guidance flagged material free cash flow dependency on iron ore volumes and cost discipline in a weak lithium price environment.

Forward guidance on capex reduction commitments, asset sale proceeds (including partial Onslow stake monetisation), and covenant headroom will be decisive for near-term re-rating; any shortfall versus debt reduction milestones or downward revision to Mining Services earnings would likely sustain bearish pressure on the stock.

announcements.headline: FY26 Financial Results Announcement
summary: Market-sensitive FY26 results release for Mineral Resources (MIN) arrives at a critical juncture — the company has been navigating significant balance sheet stress, with elevated net debt and asset divestment programs underway, making headline earnings and net debt trajectory the key metrics to watch for solvency confidence restoration.

Investors will be laser-focused on EBITDA delivery across the lithium and iron ore divisions against subdued commodity price backdrops, as well as any progress on the Onslow Iron haul road monetisation and mining services contract pipeline that underpin MIN's near-term cash generation thesis.

Forward guidance, capital allocation priorities (debt reduction vs. growth capex), and any commentary on covenants or refinancing activity will be critical signals — a credible deleveraging pathway could act as a significant re-rating catalyst given MIN's heavily discounted valuation relative to historical multiples.

announcements.headline: Full Year Statutory Accounts
summary: Full-year statutory accounts filing is a regulatory compliance milestone, but the market-sensitive flag signals material financial data — investors should scrutinise headline metrics including NPAT, EBITDA margin, and any asset impairments relative to prior guidance and consensus expectations.

As a New Zealand-listed energy generator (Genesis Energy), key watchpoints include hydrology impacts on generation output, fuel cost movements, and the performance of the Kupe gas field, all of which directly drive earnings quality and dividend sustainability for yield-focused holders.

Statutory accounts will lock in the dividend base and payout ratio for the coming year — any deviation from the ~NZD 17.0 cents per share guidance or changes to debt covenants and gearing metrics will be the critical determinant of near-term institutional positioning.

announcements.headline: Appendix 4E and 2026 Annual Report
summary: Mineral Resources' FY2026 Annual Report (Appendix 4E) is market sensitive, signalling material financial outcomes that could include significant impairments, debt restructuring updates, or earnings surprises against a backdrop of a severely challenged balance sheet and ongoing lithium price weakness that has pressured the stock throughout FY2025-26.

Investors will scrutinise net debt levels, asset carrying values (particularly lithium and iron ore operations), covenant compliance status, and any progress on the divestment program — including the Onslow haul road and other asset sales flagged as critical to deleveraging the ~$5B+ debt load.

The FY2026 result will serve as a pivotal reset moment for MIN's investment thesis: key watch items include management guidance for FY2027, the trajectory of lithium price assumptions embedded in asset valuations, and whether the board signals further capital structure initiatives (equity raise, additional asset sales, or debt refinancing) to restore financial stability.
